title: What am I doing wrong with my Claude?
author: ParkInsider
selftext:
I'm not a dev, just a hobbyist.

I started working on a few different game ideas over the past month, all rather simple. The latest one I started, I decided to ask Claude to create a mini game studio skill and apply some of the insights found here and on other forums to make the development process more smooth, but it has been everything but that.

I now work with a plugin which simulates a game studio with a producer, a visual artist, a sound artist, a programmer, a QA tester and a writer. The idea is that my feedback is ran through a "standup" committee before starting to actual get worked on. I like the idea of that feature because on my previous game ideas, my suggestions were taken at face value and implemented without any pushback, and now the committee really pushes back and provides good alternatives, and the game direction is actually great - I'm excited to play it!

However, I'm incinerating tokens like never before. I was able to get to a playable version of two other games using about one week's tokens on the $20 plan. Now, for this game, I upgraded to the $200 plan and I have burned 40% of my weekly tokens in one day, with only two prompts, mind you. Sure, lots of changes in those prompts, but still, that's kind of crazy. It seems 1-2 orders of magnitude too much.

I let the "studio" run all night, just to see what they would end up with, and the QA is still running, 9 hours in!

The game has a lot of logic, maybe I scope creeped a bit too much, but still! 9+ hours of processing?

What am I doing wrong, what should I change?

comments.author: EntropyMonkey
comments.body: Sure, learning a new tool 😂😂😂🤣🤣🤣 Learning AI is so demanding, you definitely have a head start that I'll never be able to catch up to. How many hours do I even need to invest to be able to write prompts, maybe 2 or 3? But when I use AI while also being capable of creating games independently, AI will make me a significantly better developer than people who don't have a clue could ever be 😜

replies.body:
lol if you think there's nothing to understanding the ins and outs of how models do things I suggest you learn a little bit about the tech

replies.author: EntropyMonkey
replies.body: Well, I don't really know why you think I don't know anything about AI? But it will probably shock you to hear that I use AI on a daily basis, and I probably know more about it than you do. I just simply don't need it to create games. I can do that significantly better myself. I’ve tried it, but so far the results just haven't been convincing enough for me. That said, I still try it out from time to time to see what has improved. But I don't feel like using AI is some kind of important skill that anyone couldn't just learn in a matter of a few hours

comments.author: ArthursoftDev
comments.body:
"I upgraded to the $200 plan and I have burned 40% of my weekly tokens in one day".

Honestly didn't think that was even possible atm.

I had 50 sub-agents running with ultracode the other day for \~2hours and it nocked maybe 5% of my weekly ($100 Max sub).

What effort levels have all the sub agents been set to? and which models?

One thing I do notice is Claude LOVES to write tests, then as things change the tests fail (because ofc they do) then it has to go check the failed test, find it's the test that was at fault, then update the test, then run the test again.

I do regular requests now asking Claude to optimise the tests and try reduce overheads.

Also a fan of Caveman, Ponytail, Semble (Minish Lab) and RTK (skill/plugins) that reduce conversation length, code verbosity improve code search and reduce overheads when it searches through files/text. I'd say you probably have some fundamental inefficiencies in the setup but worth taking a look at those to see if they help reduce overheads.

comments.author: Hotwingz66
comments.body: Yea, I really don't follow when I read these things.

comments.author: Jessica___
comments.body:
For me personally I just don't have these sorts of agent roles. If I want to discuss my ideas, I just have a skill for that and I chat about it with one version of Claude. For me that's enough. 

Otherwise if I have a committee of agents with different roles: do they truly have different personalities and perspectives? Or is it all just Claude dressed up in different suits? IMO it's the latter.

My workflow would just be to have different skills. One skill that tells it your writing preferences, one for your code preferences, and whatever else.

comments.body: The amount of bullshit I'm seeing lately from people who think AI is magic and can build anything is just wild.

comments.body: You are over complicating it. Many devs are. You quite literally just need claude desktop.  Go to coding tab, point to project folder and tell him what you want. Maybe at max make a gameplan and start executing it. Test what hes made and iterate one mechanic at a time. You dont need plugins or weird setups
